relationships.subject: chronic nicotine
relationships.evidence_quote: nicotine-treated mice displayed increased excitability of ACC glutamatergic neurons, presenting an increase in spike number and a decrease in rheobase

relationships.subject: chronic nicotine
relationships.evidence_quote: Compared to the vehicle control, the branch endpoints and the length of ACC microglial processes decreased in nicotine-treated mice, coinciding with the hyperactivity of glutamatergic neurons in the ACC.

relationships.subject: chronic nicotine
relationships.evidence_quote: CX3CL1 expression was increased in nicotine-treated mice compared with vehicle-treated mice

relationships.subject: ACC glutamatergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Morphological analysis of microglial cells showed that activation of microglia was effectively eliminated due to chemical inhibition of glutamatergic neurons

relationships.subject: ACC glutamatergic neurons
relationships.evidence_quote: Inhibition of ACC glutamatergic neurons alleviated nicotine-induced allodynia and reduced microglial activation.

relationships.subject: minocycline
relationships.evidence_quote: pharmacological inhibition of microglia by minocycline or liposome-clodronate reduces nicotine-induced allodynia

relationships.subject: liposome-clodronate
relationships.evidence_quote: pharmacological inhibition of microglia by minocycline or liposome-clodronate reduces nicotine-induced allodynia

relationships.subject: JMS-17-2
relationships.evidence_quote: JMS-17-2 acted as a selective small molecule inhibitor of CX3CR1 by intra-ACC injection.

relationships.subject: CX3CR1
relationships.evidence_quote: compared with nicotine-treated mice, the current-elicited action potentials decreased and rheobase increased in JMS-17-2-treated mice

relationships.subject: ACC CX3CL1
relationships.evidence_quote: The neuron-microglia interaction in chronic nicotine-induced allodynia is mediated by increased expression of neuronal CX3CL1, which activates microglia by acting on CX3CR1 receptors on microglial cells.

key_findings: Chronic oral nicotine induces allodynia with hyperexcitable ACC glutamatergic neurons and morphologically reactive but non-inflammatory ACC microglia.
Neuronal CX3CL1 acting on microglial CX3CR1 sustains ACC neuronal hyperexcitability; inhibiting microglia (minocycline, clodronate) or CX3CR1 (JMS-17-2) in ACC relieves nicotine-induced allodynia.
